data.title: Every delivery workflow reports its run in one vocabulary
The live server serves without a record and follows the run store

data.text: A stage re-entry keeps the stage's activityId, stage-<name>, takes a new attemptId and names the stage's previous attempt as supersedesAttemptId; every later state of the new attempt repeats it. The kernel also states that run.started needs --version 2 and that a version 2 run's emits each carry --event-id.
data.why: Runtime 0.8.6 refuses a new attempt of an existing activity unless it names supersedesAttemptId (Decision 10). The operator chose option 1 on 2026-11-20: no runtime change, Decision 3's stage identity kept, and the observation contract already has the rule.

data.text: The merge queue's post-merge record write fails when a lane waits on a story that this merge takes out of the queue or plan: the merge lands on the forge, but the queue journals candidate.stopped (interrupted), twice.
data.why: The validator holds a waiting lane's waitingOn to the stories still queued or planned, yet the brief has lanes wait on another lane's queued story. The merge write doesn't clear or move that wait first, so the lead must reconcile by hand and keep lanes off waitingOn.

data.text: Gap 40 named the wrong cause. When the queue merges a story whose own lane is waiting on another story and still has open work, lane_rows_after keeps the row waiting but sets waitingOn to null; state_errors then refuses the write. The merge lands on the forge, the record stays at merging, every reconcile is refused, and each serve pass journals candidate.stopped (interrupted) again.
data.why: The merge write and the reconcile both call lane_rows_after, so one lane's wait blocks the whole record until the lead moves that lane off waiting. Fix in delivery_state.lane_rows_after: keep the waitingOn of a row resting in waiting, or rest it as assigned.

data.title: Record a merge when the candidate's own lane waits on another story
data.why: The merge queue refused to record V26-3667's and V26-3666's merges in this delivery because each lane waited on another story (workflow gap 56; earlier gap 105 in V26-3645). The operator moved V26-3675 into V26-3670 on 2026-11-20 so the fix lands with this delivery.

data.note: Fix lane_rows_after so recording a merge never leaves a lane waiting with no waitingOn; the reproduction is the record's gaps/56/lane-rows-after-repro.md. Do this before V26-3669, which still waits for V26-3668 and a release candidate.
data.title: Record a merge when the candidate's own lane waits on another story

data.text: V26-3675 fixes outcome-correctness-r1-1 in this story rather than deferring it: when _return_waiting frees a row whose own queue item has merged, the row rests as the own-lane landing does (idle with nothing else open, assigned otherwise), never in its stale waitingFrom state.
data.why: It is the same failure class this story exists to fix, a merge leaving a lane's row saying something false. The lens's first proposed change stays inside _return_waiting and needs no change to how waitingFrom is stamped.

lead-wait does not wake when a planned story becomes free to start with its lane idle, though Needs you then lists it as the lead's.
data.why: The lead learns of it only by reading the live view, or as a side effect of another wake; here the operator saw V26-3669 and V26-3686 listed for the lead before the lead had recorded holds.

data.text: A Needs you row's stop tooltip shows a story title that is not the row's story: 3669 showed V26-3675's title and 3686 showed V26-3667's.
data.why: The tooltip names the wrong work, so a reader pointing at a stop to check which story it is gets another story's name.

data.text: When a queue check fails, the queue's own sync merge stays on the lane's pushed branch, so the lane's rework is no longer a fast-forward and base-merge cannot authorize that merge.
data.why: The lane must either spend another review round on a merge of a non-base commit, or the lead must force-push over the queue's commit; V26-3668 needed an operator approval and a force-with-lease push.

data.text: lead-setup --integration cuts the base only from the main checkout on the target branch, so a plan approved on its own branch must first be committed onto local main.
data.why: It forces a branch move in the shared main checkout, which other sessions use, and leaves local main ahead of origin until the integration lands.

data.text: lead-setup's clean-checkout check refuses an untracked file that setup neither reads nor writes.
data.why: Another delivery's untracked note in the shared checkout blocked setup; it had to be moved aside and restored.

data.text: lead-setup drafts each lane's owns from only its lowest-tier row in the Units and order table, dropping files later tiers name for the same lane.
data.why: Lanes would have started without the files their later stories need; the lead added V26-3668's and V26-3669's files by hand.
